hpi: Differential: Normal pressure hydrocephalus, Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, Subdural hematoma, Dementia, Other causes. Patients with normal pressure hydrocephalus can present with cognitive decline, gait disturbance, and urinary incontinence. The diagnosis is made with neuroimaging, and the treatment is a ventriculoperitoneal shunt. It is important to recognize that normal pressure hydrocephalus is treatable. It was emphasized that the lumbar puncture is the gold standard to diagnose normal pressure hydrocephalus. All of the above patients with these symptoms can be seen in the emergency department. The lumbar puncture is the definitive test for normal pressure hydrocephalus.
